# FAQ — recurring pitfalls and their solutions

### PHPUnit test failures with FFI loading errors

<!-- id=FAQ-001, date=2026-04-01, tags=phpunit ports ffi, trigger=test failures with "Failed loading .so" or "Address already in use", status=active -->

ScanMePHP has an optional C++ FFI encoder (`clib/`). The `QrReferenceTest`
suite compares the FFI encoder against a reference; if the shared library is
not built for the current platform, those tests error out. Build it first:
`cd clib && rm -rf build && cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j`.
There is no background daemon in this project, so "Address already in use" is
not a risk here (unlike the workerman-bundle workflow this was adapted from).

### Coverage is not gated in CI

<!-- id=FAQ-002, date=2026-04-01, tags=coverage phpunit, trigger=PR discussion about coverage floor, status=active -->

CI runs `composer test` (PHPUnit) without a coverage floor. Coverage requires
Xdebug or PCOV, which are not in the CI matrix (`coverage: none`). If you want
to verify coverage locally, run `vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-text` with
Xdebug enabled. Do not add a coverage gate without first deciding the floor
with the maintainer.

### FFI extension is optional but present in CI

<!-- id=FAQ-003, date=2026-04-01, tags=ffi, trigger=questions about whether ext-ffi is required, status=active -->

`ext-ffi` is enabled in CI (`setup-php` with `extensions: ffi, gd`) but is not
in `composer.json` `require` — the project is zero-runtime-dependency. The
native PHP encoder is the fallback when FFI is unavailable. Tests that require
FFI should be marked skipped when the library or extension is missing, not
failed.

### PHPStan reports `*NEVER*` or undefined `FFI\CData` property

<!-- id=FAQ-005, date=2026-04-01, tags=phpstan ffi baseline, trigger=PHPStan reports *NEVER* range errors or undefined FFI\CData property/method, status=active -->

PHPStan's range reasoning does not model QR matrix dimensions, so comparisons
in `FastEncoder` and `MaskSelector` (e.g. `>=` against a value PHPStan infers
as `*NEVER*`) produce `identical.alwaysFalse` / `greaterOrEqual.invalid` /
`booleanAnd.alwaysFalse`. These are false positives and live in
`phpstan-baseline.neon` — do not add `@phpstan-ignore` comments or widen types
to silence them; fix the source if it is a real bug, otherwise accept the
baseline entry. Separately, `FfiEncoder` accesses dynamic C struct properties
and C functions via `FFI::cdef`, which PHPStan cannot resolve — it is excluded
from analysis (see `decisions.md` DEC-005 and issue #41 for the refactor that
would bring it back). Excluding files has a cost: it hid the bugs in #39, so
prefer the refactor over a permanent exclusion.

### Zero runtime dependencies principle

<!-- id=FAQ-004, date=2026-04-01, tags=zero-deps, trigger=proposing to add a runtime dependency, status=active -->

ScanMePHP has **no external runtime dependencies** (`require` lists only
`php` and `composer-plugin-api`). PHPUnit, Paratest, ext-gd, PHPStan,
php-cs-fixer, rector and `composer/composer` (for plugin stubs) are dev/test
only and never ship. Never add anything to `require` — propose it first and
get maintainer approval.

### FFI local-build library suffix differs by platform

<!-- id=FAQ-006, date=2026-08-18, tags=ffi phpunit, trigger=FFI tests silently skip on macOS / "library not found" for a built clib, status=active -->

The local CMake build (`clib/`) produces `libscanme_qr.dylib` on macOS and
`libscanme_qr.so` on Linux, because `add_library(scanme_qr SHARED ...)` uses
the platform-default suffix with no override. Any code or test that hardcodes
`.so` for the local build path will fail to resolve on macOS and silently fall
through to the pure-PHP encoder — tests skip instead of running, masking the
problem (this was the root cause of #43, where `FfiEncoder::resolveLibraryPath()`
and the FFI test entry points all hardcoded `.so`). Always derive the suffix via
`FfiEncoder::localBuildPath()` (`PHP_OS_FAMILY === 'Darwin' ? 'dylib' : 'so'`),
the single source of truth. The vendor binary names in `PlatformDetector`/
`Composer/Plugin.php` already handle per-platform naming (arch-suffixed
`libscanme_qr-macos-<arch>.dylib`, etc.) and are a separate path — do not
conflate the two. A guard pinning that the CMake artifact suffix matches
`localBuildPath()` is tracked in #178.

### Identifying DownloadException variants — prefer codes/subclasses over message comparison

<!-- id=FAQ-007, date=2026-08-18, tags=composer exception security, trigger=writing catch logic that distinguishes a specific DownloadException factory variant (e.g. checksumMissing vs downloadFailed), status=active -->

`DownloadException` has several static factory methods (`checksumMissing`,
`downloadFailed`, `checksumMismatch`, `invalidVersion`, `ffiNotAvailable`).
When catch logic needs to branch on a specific variant, do **not** compare
`$e->getMessage()` to the factory's output — it works only while the format
string and arguments stay byte-identical, and silently breaks (wrong catch
branch, missing remediation hint) the moment a future refactor adds context
to the message. Prefer an exception code constant
(`public const CODE_CHECKSUM_MISSING = 1;` checked via `getCode()`), a
dedicated subclass caught by type, or an `isChecksumMissing(): bool` method.
The current Plugin catch blocks (`src/Composer/Plugin.php`) use the fragile
string-equality form and are tracked for hardening by #184.

### Build commands must not merge stderr into captured output

<!-- id=FAQ-008, date=2026-08-19, tags=security ffi exception, trigger=writing exec()/shell_exec() calls in src/Builder.php or any build-step code that forwards output via exception messages, status=active -->

Never append `2>&1` to a command in `src/Builder.php` (or any build step) if
the captured output may reach callers via exception messages. Compiler and
diagnostic stderr routinely contains absolute local paths and environment
details, which becomes an information leak when concatenated into a thrown
message. Use a single `exec()` with the array parameter for stdout-only
capture and surface only a sanitised `BuildException` factory message (exit
code, `basename()` of paths); let stderr go to the process's own stderr for
CLI/CI diagnostics. `Builder::runCommand()` is the single seam for any future
structured logging. Root cause of #57; guarded by
`tests/BuilderTest.php::testBuildExceptionFactoriesAreSanitised`, a dataProvider
that asserts no `2>&1` and no absolute path in any of the four factory messages.

### BuildException factories are the only sanctioned throw from Builder

<!-- id=FAQ-009, date=2026-08-19, tags=exception ffi, trigger=writing a throw statement inside src/Builder.php, status=active -->

`Builder::build()` must throw `BuildException` via its static factories
(`toolsNotAvailable`, `cmakeFailed`, `buildFailed`, `libraryNotFound`), never
a bare `\RuntimeException` with concatenated raw output. The factories produce
sanitised messages (fixed string + exit code, or `basename()` of the build
dir) so no local path or compiler output reaches the caller. `BuildException
extends \RuntimeException`, so existing `catch (\RuntimeException)` /
`catch (\Exception)` (e.g. `src/Composer/InstallScript.php`) stays compatible.
To distinguish variants, use an exception code/subclass or an `is*(): bool`
method, not `getMessage()` comparison (see FAQ-007). The same convention
applies to other Builder-adjacent code that currently throws bare
`\RuntimeException` (tracked separately).

### Stubbed downloaders in Composer-plugin tests must fail, not overwrite

<!-- id=FAQ-010, date=2026-08-19, tags=tests composer security, trigger=writing a stub or mock for BinaryDownloader in tests/Composer/, status=active -->

A stub downloader used to exercise `Plugin`'s install orchestration must
(1) **throw** instead of writing content, (2) honor the directory passed to
`createDownloader()` — it is called once per install path (`ext-binaries`
and `ffi-binaries`) — and (3) count calls **per instance** before asserting
`=== 1`. A success-writing stub silently masks a missing `@unlink` in the
mismatch branch (overwrite makes the file exist regardless), and asserts a
happy end the real checksum path would reject. Because CI always enables ffi
(FAQ-003) and the FFI fallback reuses `createDownloader()` with a different
directory, a single fixed-directory stub makes call counts
environment-dependent. Learned in the #185 cycle (PR #192): the committed
orchestration tests use `FailingStubBinaryDownloader` plus a factory closure
in `tests/Composer/PluginTest.php`; both the ext and FFI unlink branches are
mutation-proven red when their `@unlink` is removed.

### Mirrored install branches each need their own planted regression test

<!-- id=FAQ-011, date=2026-08-19, tags=tests security composer, trigger=writing a regression test for one of the two mirrored branches in src/Composer/Plugin.php (extension vs FFI install), status=active -->

`Plugin::installExtensionBinary()` and `installFfiBinary()` are mirrored
branches: a regression test planting a fixture on one side (tampered file,
directory at target path) does NOT pin the other side. Proven twice in the
#185 cycle (PR #192): the FFI mismatch branch had no committed test at all
(F-9), and after the ext-only directory test was added, the FFI `is_file()`
guard still passed the whole suite with a directory at the target path
(F-11, empirically probed). For every planted/branch test, mirror it on the
second branch with the environment skip it needs (`extension_loaded('ffi')`,
and skip when `scanmeqr` is preloaded).
